subject: Shit To Do in NYC (Oct 5): Honey Dijon all day, Balanchine at night
opener: Three-day weekend, and the city noticed: Knockdown goes fourteen hours, Good Room gets the only US stop of RA's anniversary tour, and Sunday is a free day because Monday is a holiday. Pick your damage early, because the good rooms this week are small.

picks.headline: Honey Dijon takes Knockdown, 3pm to 5am
picks.title: Honey Dijon: Day & Night
picks.when: Sat Oct 10, 3pm to 5am; starts outdoors in The Ruins, ends in the Main Hall
picks.why: This is the day-party-into-warehouse format you already know you love, except the person behind the decks spent thirty years actually building house music. Start outside in The Ruins at four with daylight and a beer, let it move inside, leave whenever your body says so. Derrick Carter and Luke Solomon are the support, which is absurd for a Saturday afternoon.
picks.heads_up: 21+, tickets on RA and DICE, and RA isn't listing a price. Fourteen hours is a trap; go early for The Ruins and treat the Main Hall close as optional.
picks.invite_text: Honey Dijon is doing fourteen hours at Knockdown on Saturday starting at 3. I'm going for the outdoor half around 4, come find me.

verification.note: Read the RA event page: Sat, Oct 10, 2026, 15:00-05:00 at Knockdown Center, Honey Dijon with Luke Solomon/Anastazja in The Ruins and Derrick Carter in the Main Hall; the promoter blurb's '10/8' is a typo, the listing date field says Oct 10; no price shown (RA ticket widget), 21+.

picks.headline: RA's 25th tour, one night, Good Room
picks.title: RA25 World Tour: New York (Nick León, Galcher Lustwerk, Stacey Hotwaxx Hale b2b Kilopatrah Jones)
picks.why: Ten dates worldwide and New York gets one, in a 600-cap Greenpoint club instead of a shed. Nick León headlining with Galcher Lustwerk and Stacey Hotwaxx Hale b2b Kilopatrah Jones is a lineup nobody outside the scene is tracking. Both floors, Friday, and you can see everyone's face.
picks.heads_up: Tickets through RA and there's still one unannounced name on the bill. This is the kind of one-stop booking that goes quietly and then is gone.
picks.invite_text: Resident Advisor's 25th anniversary tour has exactly one New York night and it's Friday at Good Room. Nick León headlining, both floors. In?

verification.note: Read RA's own announcement (ra.co/news/86003): Friday October 9, Nick Leon, Galcher Lustwerk, adobeprincess, Stacey Hotwaxx Hale b2b Kilopatrah Jones, Baalti take over both floors at Good Room, Greenpoint; the article publishes no start time or ticket price.

picks.headline: ZickZack, the German punk label, on Essex Street
picks.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack & the Invention of the German Underground
picks.when: opening reception Thu Oct 8, 6-8pm; gallery hours Thursday-Sunday 3-8pm
picks.why: First show ever mounted outside Germany about Alfred Hilsberg and ZickZack, the Hamburg label that put out Einstürzende Neubauten and basically invented the Neue Deutsche Welle underground. Rare records, flyers, badges, Super-8. It's a gallery you could cross in ten steps, run by the Goethe-Institut with no marketing budget, which is the exact register you keep asking for.
picks.heads_up: Opening reception is Thursday 6 to 8pm. If Thursday is spoken for, the show runs through Nov 7 with gallery hours Thursday to Sunday, 3 to 8pm. The 6pm event on the 8th is an opening reception, not a talk, and after that the gallery is only open Thursday to Sunday, 3-8pm.
picks.invite_text: Thursday there's an opening on the Lower East Side for the German punk label that put out Einstürzende Neubauten. Rare records and flyers, tiny room, 6 to 8. Drinks after.

verification.note: Goethe-Institut USA listing and its event page (event_id 27324564) show the exhibition runs 10/08-11/07/2026 at Various/Artists, 19 Essex St; gallery hours Thu-Sun 3-8pm and an opening reception Thursday October 8, 6-8pm (no talk listed, no admission price stated).

picks.headline: Balanchine and Robbins, Koch Theater, two nights
picks.title: New York City Ballet: Masters at Work I
picks.when: Fri Oct 9 to Sat Oct 10, evening performances both nights, about 2 hours 10 minutes
picks.address: 20 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
picks.why: The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center is still your favorite night in the city, and this is the same company in the same house without waiting until December. Three works, pianist onstage, about two hours ten. The Concert is Robbins being genuinely funny, so she isn't sitting through an hour of abstraction to get to the good part.
picks.heads_up: Friday and Saturday evenings only, and these are the last two outings before the fall season closes Oct 18. Book the sitter first, tickets second.
picks.invite_text: Got an idea for Friday: City Ballet at the Koch, three Balanchine and Robbins pieces, ends early enough for a drink after. Want me to get the sitter?

verification.note: NYCB's own program page lists Masters at Work I as SEPT 29, 30, OCT 3 mat & eve, 9, 10 eve at the David H. Koch Theater, approx. 2 hr 10 min; page metadata gives 19:30 curtain for the evening shows; no prices listed on the page.

picks.headline: The George Lucas Talk Show at Littlefield
picks.title: The George Lucas Talk Show
picks.why: Connor Ratliff interviews real guests in character as a retired George Lucas, with a sidekick named Watto, and has been doing it long enough that it's become its own small institution. Cult comedy with a committed bit beats a club with a two-drink minimum every time. Gowanus, Thursday, doors at seven.
picks.heads_up: 21+, show at 8pm, and the guests get announced close to showtime, so book on faith. Parklife is right there afterward.
picks.invite_text: Thursday: the George Lucas Talk Show at Littlefield, guy does a whole fake George Lucas late-night thing with real guests. Doors at 7, drinks after.

verification.note: Littlefield's own event page states October 8, 2026, 8:00pm-11:00pm, doors 7:00pm, 21+, tickets $18.71-$29.50.

picks.headline: A RÜFÜS DU SOL night inside a sauna
picks.title: Deep Listening Night: RÜFÜS DU SOL
picks.why: One night, one catalog, the entire Othership sound system given over to RÜFÜS DU SOL start to finish. Melodic house with real low end is your core lane, and this plays it at 185 degrees with ice baths between rounds instead of a club floor. Friday night out, no bar, home at a reasonable hour.
picks.heads_up: 9pm to 11:30pm, booked as a timed session so capacity is tiny and it sells out. Flatiron location, not Williamsburg.
picks.invite_text: Friday night: Othership is playing nothing but RÜFÜS DU SOL through the sauna for two and a half hours, ice baths in between. Weird and good. Booking two spots.

verification.note: Othership's event page states Friday, Oct 9, 9:00 PM - 11:30 PM EDT at Othership Flatiron; no price shown (booking goes through the schedule page).

picks.headline: Roman Flügel in the Public Records nursery
picks.title: The Nursery: Frank & Tony with Roman Flügel
picks.why: Public Records opens the outdoor nursery on Sunday afternoon for Frank & Tony and Roman Flügel, a Frankfurt lifer with thirty years of records behind him. Best sound in Brooklyn, fifteen minutes from your door, outdoors in October while that's still possible. Holiday Monday means a 3pm start doesn't cost you anything.
picks.heads_up: Outdoors, so dress for a Gowanus afternoon turning cold. Tickets via DICE; it's a small space and the long-weekend Sunday crowd will find it.
picks.invite_text: Sunday afternoon at Public Records, outdoor nursery, Roman Flügel playing from 3. Holiday Monday so there's no reason not to. Come through.

verification.note: The DICE link would not load, but Public Records' own calendar lists 'Sun 10.11, Club, 3:00 pm, The Nursery - The Nursery: Frank & Tony, Roman Flugel'; no price published on the venue calendar.

radar.heads_up: Could not re-check the listing page this morning. Confirm the date on the link before you buy.

anytime.headline: Limousine in Greenpoint has a private karaoke room
anytime.title: Limousine, new cocktail bar with a private karaoke room
anytime.why: From the Five Leaves and Goldie's team, in the old Ponyboy space: black banquettes, a real cocktail list, snacks until midnight, and a karaoke room you can book. That's a plan, not a 'grab a drink' text.

verification.note: The Infatuation's new-openings guide lists Limousine as open at 632 Manhattan Ave, Greenpoint - a cocktail bar in the former Ponyboy space from the Five Leaves/Goldie's team with a rentable private karaoke room and small bites until midnight.

anytime.headline: Cmarty's jerk pop-up inside King Tai
anytime.title: Cmarty's Jerk pop-up inside King Tai
anytime.why: A Jamaican-American jerk kitchen running out of a small Crown Heights bar: jerk banh mi, bourbon wings, pork shu mai, menu changes on the cook's whim. Restaurant-inside-a-bar, walkable-ish from Fort Greene, Wednesday through Friday evenings.
anytime.heads_up: Cmarty's is only inside King Tai Wednesday through Friday evenings, not earlier in the week.

verification.note: The Infatuation's current best-pop-ups guide lists 'Cmarty's Jerk @ King Tai / Wednesdays 5-11pm; Thursdays & Fridays, 5-9pm' at 1095 Bergen St, Crown Heights; the linked 2024 review still says Monday to Friday, so the guide supersedes it.

anytime.headline: The Tiny Cupboard, stand-up every night in Bushwick
anytime.title: The Tiny Cupboard
anytime.when: shows nightly; Sun–Thu typically 8pm & 9:30pm (plus 11pm open mic), Fri/Sat 7pm, 8:30pm & 10:15pm
anytime.price: $13.50 + $2.41 fee online Sun–Thu ($20 at the door); Fri/Sat shows $19.50 + $2.82 fee online, $25 at the door
anytime.why: A rooftop room and a small indoor room, shows every single night, thirteen bucks online and no drink minimum. There's a board game and video game bar out back so the night keeps going without a second venue. This is your 48-hours-notice answer in Bushwick.
anytime.heads_up: Weeknight shows are the $13.50 ones; Friday and Saturday shows run $19.50 online and $25 at the door.

verification.note: Read thetinycupboard.com/calendar (Oct 2026): the club at 10 Cooper St, Brooklyn has stand-up every night through the email window (Oct 5–11 all listed), with $13.50 + $2.41 fee / $20 door on Sun–Thu, but Fri 10/9 and Sat 10/10 prime shows are $19.50 + $2.82 fee with $25 at the door, so the price line needed correcting; 'anytime' is right since it is an ongoing nightly venue.

family.headline: Fall festival at Lakeside, Prospect Park
family.title: Fall Festival at Lakeside, Prospect Park
family.when: Sat Oct 10 to Sun Nov 1, weekends from 11am; go in the late morning
family.price: varies by activity — check the Lakeside page
family.why: Pumpkins, hay bales, carnival games and seasonal food at the LeFrak Center, opening this weekend from 11am. It's flat and paved, so the stroller rolls straight in, and you can be out by early afternoon before the nap collapse. Skip the haunted hotel walkthrough, that's for bigger kids.
family.invite_text: Saturday late morning: the fall thing at Lakeside in Prospect Park opens, pumpkins and hay bales and food. Stroller-easy and we'd be home by two.

verification.note: Lakeside's own Fall Festival page: Oct 8 - Nov 1, 2026 at LeFrak Center at Lakeside, 171 East Drive, weekend hours 11:00AM-10:00PM (so Sat Oct 10 is open from 11am), closed Tuesdays/Wednesdays Oct 13-14 and 20-21; pricing as listed.

notes: Thin on Afrobeats and dancehall this week, which is annoying given where your listening is; the Halloween amapiano stuff is all later in October, so it's on the radar instead. Left the new Williamsburg steakhouse out because it opens on a Tuesday and that's not a night worth spending, and skipped Mister Sunday and Petite Rouge since the Sunday date is in dispute and Company XIV already went out last month.
